figure_candidates.label: Figure 1
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 1. Introducing a photobiocatalytic “redox buffering” strategy to enable direct C(sp3)−H radical alkylation. (A) Typical reductive hydro-
functionalization reported in non-natural photobiocatalysis. (B) Natural redox buffering system. (C) This work: direct C(sp3)−H bond radical
hydroalkylation is enabled by synergistic integration of oxidant and reductant. LG, leaving group; ERED, ene-reductase; KRED, ketoreductase;
NAD(P)H, the reduced form of nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (phosphate); FMNsq, semiquinone form of flavin mononucleotide; HAT,
hydrogen atom transfer; Ox, oxidant; PG, protecting group; IRED, imine reductase; and PC, photocatalyst.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 2. Reaction development. (A) Model reaction and conditions variation. (B) Molecular docking of product 3a onto the structure of IRED1.
(C) 96-well plate-based photobiocatalytic setup, illuminating with 420−430 nm LEDs. (D) Trajectory of evolution. a15% v/v DMSO was used as
cosolvent; bconditions: 1a (0.008 mmol), 2a (0.08 mmol), HAT reagent (0.024 mmol, 3 equiv), imine reductase (0.5 mol %), Ir(ppy)3 (2 mol %),
GDH (4 U/mL), NADP+ (15 mol %), glucose (0.04 mmol, 5 equiv), 5% v/v DMSO, and 10% v/v MeOH in HEPES buffer (100 mM, pH 8.0)
were stirred for 16 h under a N2 atmosphere with irradiation of 500−510 nm LEDs, total volume of the reaction is 2.0 mL; cyield was determined
by GC; denantiomeric excess value (ee) was determined by HPLC analysis on a chiral stationary phase; HAT, hydrogen atom transfer; GDH,
glucose dehydrogenase; NADP+, the oxidized form of nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate; and Glu, glucose. n.a. = not applicable.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 3. Scope investigation. Standard conditions: enamide 1 (0.008 mmol, 1 equiv), alkane 2 (0.08 mmol, 10 equiv), HAT reagent-1 (0.024
mmol, 3 equiv), IREDHAT (0.5 mol %), Ir(ppy)3 (2 mol %), GDH (4 U/mL), NADP+ (15 mol %), glucose (0.04 mmol, 5 equiv), 5% v/v DMSO,
and 10% v/v MeOH in HEPES buffer (100 mM, pH 8.0) were stirred for 16 h under a N2 atmosphere with irradiation of 500−510 nm LEDs, total
volume of the reaction is 2.0 mL; aisolated yield based on a 0.3 mmol reaction, and 0.2 mol % enzyme and 5 mol % NADP+ were used; b10% v/v
DMSO as cosolvent; cIRED1-T123F-S67T was used; and dIRED1-T123F was used. Duplicated runs using different batches of enzyme yielded
results within ±5% error in yield and within ±1% error in ee. The absolute configuration of 3r obtained was assigned by the comparison of
retention time on HPLC with the enantiopure standard (R)-3r.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 4
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 4. Mechanistic studies. (A) Radical trap experiment. (B) Monitoring the reactions with or without IREDHAT. (C) Stern−Volmer quenching
studies. (D) Isotope labeling experiments. (E) Kinetic isotope effect experiments.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 5
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 5. Proposed catalytic cycle. GDH, glucose dehydrogenase; NADP+, the oxidized form of nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate; Glu,
glucose; and HAT, hydrogen atom transfer. The dot curve represents the protein scaffold.
